sponger noun

also parasite (person), hanger-on, freeloader, scrounger, toady

classical

Plaut. Men. 505: Tuom parasītum nōn nōvistī?
Cic. Lael. 98: parasītōrum in cōmoediīs assentātiō (Lewis & Short)

parasītus, parasītī m.

noun, second declension

one who lives at another’s table by flattery and jokes; a sponger

Greek παράσιτος, “one who eats beside another”. A stock character of comedy.

Examples

  • Tuom parasītum nōn nōvistī?

    Don’t you know your own sponger?Plaut. Men. 505

  • quasi mūrēs semper edimus aliēnum cibum

    like mice, we are always eating other people’s foodPlaut. Capt. 77

See also guest, uninvited, flatter, glutton.

SourcesLewis & Short: parasitus

Plautus, Captivi 77; Menaechmi 505.
